conviction_note: Near non-result: the Q3 release is new numbers on a 21-analyst mega-cap, but GSK's own 8 Oct aide-memoire already told the market that Q3 core profit takes the Nuvalent costs and interest, a tough tax comparator (16.0% in Q3 2025) and a worse FX hit on profit than on sales; consensus has come down to that (Q3 ADR EPS $1.33 from $1.41 90 days ago). What is left is a mild upward lean from a 4-for-4 core EPS beat record and the chance of a narrowed or nudged-up FY guide, against a name that sold a clean Q1 beat by 5.4% on an unchanged guide and has run about 10% off its 8 Oct low into the print. So p_up 51 on an abs move of 5.0 gives +0.1. impact_sum (+0.3) and the scaled number agree in sign and are both small.

findings.finding: GSK's own Q3 aide-memoire pre-signals a weak Q3 for core profit growth: Nuvalent cost consolidation and acquisition interest, a tough tax comparator (core tax 16.0% in Q3 2025 against about 17.5% guided for FY2026), and an FX hit on core OP larger than the roughly -1% on sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026 GSK beat on core EPS (+4.9% vs estimate) and fell 5.42% because the guide was only reiterated, so the reported quarter alone has not carried the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is priced. The company published this itself, and the Q3 EPS consensus has already been cut about 6% over 90 days (from $1.41 to $1.33). If it were not priced, consensus would still sit near the year-ago $1.46. The only residual is whether analysts fully cut for the tax and FX effects.

findings.finding: GSK has beaten core EPS consensus in each of the last four quarters (+16.8%, +11.2%, +4.9%, +7.1%), and this quarter's bar has been lowered by about 6% in 90 days, so a fifth core EPS beat is the base-rate outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats moved the stock both ways: FY2025 +6.91% (with a new guide), Q1 2026 -5.42% (beat with an unchanged guide), Q2 2026 +3.47% (beat with an upper-half specification).
findings.why_not_priced: A habitual beater's beat is largely expected by 21 analysts. What is left is the downward drift in the bar. If it were fully priced, a beat would not have produced a +3.5% day in July; the Q1 sale shows that the guide line decides.
findings.independence: The beat history is in the sealed baseline (Yahoo earningsHistory), a different source from the consensus-drift article: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v10/finance/quoteSummary/GSK.L?modules=earningsHistory%2CfinancialData

findings.finding: Vaccines face a tough Q3 comparator the company itself flagged (Q3 2025 had Arexvy tenders in Canada and Spain, German reimbursement, and a one-off Priorix bulk antigen sale; Q2 2026 vaccines were flattered by 3ppt of prior-period rebate adjustments; US Shingrix demand is lower), and RBC expects weak vaccines, especially Shingrix.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Vaccines and Shingrix misses have historically weighed on GSK prints; the 2026 prints were driven by the guide rather than by vaccines.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company flagged the comparator and the sell-side preview already expects vaccine weakness offset by HIV and Nucala. The residual is only the size of the Shingrix US shortfall, for which no independent series was found.

findings.finding: H1 2026 turnover ran at +5% CER, the top of the 3-5% FY range, and core EPS at +9% against a 7-9% guide; RBC (via Proactive) says GSK may narrow its full-year guidance, which on the H1 run-rate would tilt toward the upper end rather than down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide line moves this name: FY2025 new guide +6.91%, Q1 2026 reiteration -5.42%, Q2 2026 upper-half specification +3.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. The upper-half specification is already out, but a further narrowing or a turnover nudge-up is not, and the stock has given back gains after July (from 2007p on 29 Jul to 1735.5p on 8 Oct before recovering). If an upgrade were fully expected, the preview would not frame it as a possibility. This is an inference from the run-rate, not a company signal, so it stays small.

baseline_tension: Broadly agrees: the lean (+0.33, mostly a small-short 'squeeze' component that is weak on a mega-cap) and the +3.2% 20-day run-up both point mildly up, as do the findings; the run of about 10% off the 8 Oct low on pipeline approvals raises the bar for a plain reiteration, which is why p_up stays at 51.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry; the one domestic primary document of value (GSK's Q3 aide-memoire on gsk.com) is in the same English the sell-side reads, and UK retail previews were not reachable
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the company-flagged Q3 phasing finding went from -0.2 to -0.1, and the vaccine-comparator finding (also from the aide-memoire) from -0.2 to -0.1
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' plus this name selling its Q1 beat: the beat-base-rate finding went from +0.3 to +0.2, and p_up stayed at 51

'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and 'size on what is new': abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.0, toward GSK's own 5.4 median, because the quarter is not pre-released and a guide narrowing is possible
